rules.name: Use a more precise contextual word when needed
rules.guidance: Replace a word only when the alternative is a closer fit for the intended meaning, discipline, and sentence context. Prefer familiar, precise academic language over decorative or unnecessarily complex vocabulary.
apply_when: A word is vague, inaccurate, awkward, or inconsistent with the concept it describes.
do_not_apply_when: The original word is already accurate.
The proposed alternative only changes style without improving meaning or clarity.
The alternative changes technical meaning, certainty, emphasis, or scope.
preservation: Do not choose a synonym merely to make text look different.
Keep domain-specific terms when they are the correct terms.

rules.name: Reduce distracting local repetition
rules.guidance: When the same non-technical word is repeated close together and the repetition distracts from reading, consider a contextually accurate alternative or remove a genuinely redundant occurrence.
apply_when: A non-essential word or phrase is repeated nearby without adding emphasis or precision.
do_not_apply_when: Repetition is needed for clarity, terminology consistency, emphasis, or formal structure.
A synonym would be less precise.
preservation: Never vary a technical term solely to avoid repetition.

rules.name: Maintain consistent technical terminology
rules.guidance: Use the same term for the same concept throughout a document unless the source intentionally distinguishes concepts.
apply_when: A concept is named inconsistently and equivalence is certain.
do_not_apply_when: Terms may represent different components, methods, or metrics.
preservation: Never replace a domain term with a loose synonym.
